handoff: Data and Event Platform implemented and tested: canonical versioned EventEnvelope (UUIDv7, UTC, trusted organization_id / explicit global scope, correlation/causation, strict typed payload), deterministic injection-safe subject taxonomy nxs.<env>.<scope>.<domain>.<event>, event schema/version decoder registry with fail-closed unknown-type and unsupported-version handling.

PostgreSQL transactional outbox (event_outbox, TENANT-OWNED, forced RLS + nxs_system_relay unscoped policy): the outbox row and the business mutation commit atomically; WITH CHECK makes a forged organization_id impossible; the relay claims rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, takes a crash-recovering lease, publishes to JetStream, checks the ack, then marks PUBLISHED.

JetStream transport extends the P01 messaging boundary: every publish ack checked under a bounded timeout, event_id is the broker dedup identity, no silent fallback to core NATS, hardened environments fail closed without durable JetStream. Global platform events publish directly through the same confirmed path.

Durable pull-consumer framework: explicit ack only after the handler effect and the PostgreSQL idempotency receipt commit; retryable failures NAK with bounded exponential backoff; terminal failures are recorded (event_dead_letters + dead-letter subject), TERMed and never hot-looped; bounded concurrency/ack-wait/handler-timeout; graceful drain.

Consumer idempotency (consumer_receipts, PLATFORM-INTERNAL): (consumer_name, event_id) claim in the same transaction as the handler effect. Duplicate delivery, lost ACK, redelivery and two concurrent deliveries all resolve to exactly one business effect (proven with real PostgreSQL + JetStream).

Delivery semantics documented precisely: Nexus AI guarantees at-least-once transport; exactly-once transport is NOT claimed; idempotent consumers are required for duplicate-safe business effects. ADR-0047 / ADR-0048 / ADR-0049 + docs/engineering/events.md.
